name: Benjamin
overview: Benjamin is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Harim who had married a foreign wife, as noted in Ezra 10:32. While his tribal affiliation is not explicitly stated here, he is known biblically as the youngest son of Jacob and Rachel. No additional personal notes are provided in this record.
namesAndTitles: The name Benjamin means 'son of [the] right hand; southerner' according to Ezra 10:32. This proper name was not given directly by God but carries significance related to position and perhaps geographical orientation.
familyAndRelationships: Benjamin is explicitly recorded as a descendant of Harim, as stated in Ezra 10:32. Beyond this connection, Scripture does not provide further family relationships for this individual within the given data.
scriptureSignificance: Benjamin holds importance as the youngest son of Jacob, born during the death of his mother Rachel, and was deeply cherished by his father. He is the progenitor of the tribe of Benjamin, which played a prominent role in Israel's history by producing the first king, Saul, and the apostle Paul. This tribe also maintained loyalty to Judah during the kingdom's division, underscoring Benjamin's lasting legacy in biblical history.
